_readme: Jobs, houses and money. Numbers here are the main balance levers.

jobs: label, cat (rest / staff / escort), energy (weekly cost), skill (which skill she uses), needs (amenity required), room (uses a bedroom), must (must-offer role: she serves propositions from her menu and expects them; other jobs choose, see data/balance.json → props), desc. jobTrust: trust she needs for a job she doesn't particularly like. Removed jobs: companion (now courtesan), reception (now promoter).

slots: positions per house. Keys: base, amenity ids (bar, stage, guard, bath), perSize (one more per N building size), perRoom (per bedroom), min / perRooms (one per N bedrooms, at least min), as (same number as another job). A job with no entry (promoter, maid) is unlimited. Courtesans: 2 + bedrooms; attendants: one per courtesan position.

propRate / propWhere: base chance per client visit that a staff job gets propositioned, and where it happens (reports). The bar, her propRate fx and her appeal multiply it. Courtesans are asked through the normal client flow (balance.json → jobs.propWant), so their entry is 0.

classes: client classes; mult = how much they pay; wants = how much more (or less) often they ask for a service, by service id; tech = mean technique (0.3-1.4); prop = chance a visiting client of this class makes a proposition to staff; rowdy = chance of bar trouble; reckless = how reckless/forceful (adds half to pushy; a Bar adds more); pushy = chance to try to force it after hearing no. tier: the old four classes (commoner, adventurer, merchant, noble) that houses' clientele weights (houses cls, 4 numbers) and ladies' classBonus/classLike fall back to; share: weight within its tier; traits: x weights for client traits (balance.json → clients.traits) for this class. stats = {stat: weight} stat taste (balance.json → clients.statPref): his draw, satisfaction and fee follow how high her stats are. Regulars keep their class taste.

upgrades with a "race" field are race houses (tether = spirits, charger = androids, chapel = angels, sigil = demons; the garden, incense burner, workshop, laundry, classroom have no race). amenity effect numbers are in balance.json → amenities. Races with "needs" in races.json can't be recruited into or moved to a house without that upgrade. upgrades.mood (race houses): weekly mood bonus for ladies of that race working or living in the house.

beds / floorRest: staff beds and how much they rest. amenitySize: building space each amenity takes (0 = takes no room). decor: house décor tiers (h.decor, label / cost; demand and upkeep per tier are in balance.json → amenities.decor). drinks: the bar's drinks menu tiers (h.drinks 0-3, needs the Bar, no room; income and proposition multipliers and upkeep per tier are in balance.json → amenities.drinks). classroom + teacher job: one teacher per house teaches a skill (h.teachSkill, null = her best tech skill) to the others (balance.json → amenities.classroom). A job with "race" is only for that race. An upgrade with "needs" requires another upgrade built first. racePerks: shown on sheets (the effects live in data/races.json and code).
roomMult / roomNames / roomTierCost: client room tiers. prices: house price levels (mult = fee multiplier, demand = client multiplier).

houses: every house. cls = clientele weights [commoner, adventurer, merchant, noble]. npc = the named lady who comes with it (characters.json). setting = image backdrop. starter = pickable at the start; premium houses unlock with level / renown.
pasts: Sam's past lives at the start; sam = his starting stat bonuses. Other past perks (cook's free dinners, massage training bonus) are in code.
upgrades.mood (race houses): weekly mood bonus for ladies of that race working or living in the house.
hauntRep (haunted houses): reputation at which the haunting stops scaring clients off (demand ramps from 45% to 125% of normal by then; default 40).
lodging: weekly room-and-board income from travelers, x(1 + rep/50). sat: flat satisfaction bonus for every client (a welcoming house).
tiers: the four client tiers, in the order of houses → cls. Host (job host): entertains clients waiting for a courtesan; see balance.json → clients.wait / clients.host.

madame.label: Madame
madame.desc: Runs the house: calmer moods, clients matched to the right lady, and coaching for courtesans she out-ranks in popularity and skill. Steps in for overwhelmed courtesans; can be propositioned.

promoter.label: Promoter
promoter.desc: Draws clients in. With free samples the draw is bigger, but it tires her and shows in the house's reputation. Unlimited positions.

attendant.label: Attendant
attendant.desc: The madame's and courtesans' assistant: courtesans tire less and their clients are happier; a courtesan with her own attendant is happier and trusts the house more. Learns from the madame. Steps in when the courtesans are swamped. Doesn't expect propositions, though some clients expect her to offer.

security.label: Security
security.desc: Walks troublemakers out and handles pushy clients. Builds trust.

bartender.label: Bartender
bartender.desc: Sells drinks. Needs a Bar. The house gets more propositions, more rowdiness and more reckless clients.

dancer.label: Dancer
dancer.desc: Draws crowds, earns tips, builds popularity. Expects propositions and serves them from her menu.

bath.label: Bath Attendant
bath.desc: Tends the bathhouse; always offers bathers a massage. Expects propositions and serves them from her menu.

teacher.label: Teacher
teacher.desc: Teaches one subject (a trade skill or a service, chosen below) to every lady in the house who is behind her in it. Humans learn faster. Takes no clients. One position.

maid.label: Maid
maid.desc: Keeps the house tidy (tidiness drives reputation, mood and rest). Wears a maid uniform while on the job. Unlimited positions.

chapel.label: Chapel Keeper
chapel.desc: Angels only. Tends the Quiet Chapel: visitors come to her for comfort, not for service. Adds reputation and popularity, and visitors leave donations. Two positions.

courtesan.label: Courtesan
courtesan.desc: Offers her service menu to everyone. Lowest comfort lines, can work when not in the mood. Uses a room for services.

host.label: Host
host.desc: Keeps clients company while they wait for a courtesan: conversation, drinks, and a little warming up for those open to it (light services out in the lounge, never to the finish). A skilled host keeps people waiting longer and happier. Can be propositioned, which takes her off the floor for a while.

decor.label: Bare walls
decor.desc: Plain plaster and whatever the last owner left.

decor.label: Lanterns and a signboard
decor.desc: Warm lamps by the door and a sign people can actually read.

decor.label: Paintings and drapes
decor.desc: Framed paintings, heavy curtains, a proper entrance hall.

decor.label: Gilded décor
decor.desc: Gilt mirrors, chandeliers and a doorman's carpet. Nobles take notice.

drinks.label: House ale
drinks.desc: Watered-down ale and whatever is in the cask.

drinks.label: Good wine
drinks.desc: A proper wine list and clean glasses.

drinks.label: Imported vintages
drinks.desc: Cellared vintages from across the sea, poured by the glass.

drinks.label: Dwarven spirits & elven wine
drinks.desc: Rare spirits and moon-ripened wine. Patrons linger, spend and get ideas.

human.label: Adaptable
human.desc: Trust, skills, stats and lewdness grow 25% faster; learns 50% more in the classroom. Signing bonuses are 20% lower.

elf.label: Long-lived
elf.desc: Mood changes slowly and settles slowly, for better and worse. Nobles pay 20% more, merchants 5%. Thrives in a garden.

beastkin.label: Simple needs
beastkin.desc: Asks for 15% lower wages, recovers 15% more energy and her lewdness grows 15% faster. Gets restless sooner, feels incense more strongly, and takes it hard when Sam turns her down.

demon.label: Feeds on desire
demon.desc: Services cost 40% less energy, and clients who finish feed her. Sleep does little for her and a working week burns energy. Restless, she can drain a client dry. Higher lust ceiling (+20), lust builds 30% faster.

dwarf.label: Hardy
dwarf.desc: +25 max energy, recovers 25% more from rest, builds lust 25% more slowly. Bartends 15% better. A house with a Workshop gets cheaper to improve while dwarves live there.

spirit.label: Incorporeal
spirit.desc: Needs no bed, but needs a Tethering Stone to live here. Recovers a steady amount every week. Moods swing hard but settle fast. Adventurers pay 30% more and seek her out.

angel.label: Serene
angel.desc: Lower lust ceiling (-30), never reckless, resting mood +5. Can keep a Quiet Chapel (Chapel Keeper). Nobles are especially fond of her.

android.label: Rechargeable
android.desc: Needs a Charging Alcove and no bed. Rest charges her to full, but each recharge costs the house a fee. Skills grow 25% faster, +10 max energy, bad moods hit 40% softer, lust builds slowly. Merchants pay 20% more.

guard.label: Guard Post
guard.desc: Security is much more effective. Takes no room.

bath.label: Bathhouse
bath.desc: +mood, +satisfaction. Unlocks Bath Attendant job and bath scenes.

tether.label: Tethering Stone
tether.desc: Spirits can live and work here. Takes 1 room; while one stands (in any house), spirit candidates turn up more often.

charger.label: Charging Alcove
charger.desc: Androids can live and work here. Recharge fee -40%. Takes 1 room; while one stands (in any house), android candidates turn up more often.

chapel.label: Quiet Chapel
chapel.desc: Angel mood +4. Unlocks the Chapel Keeper job (angels only, 2 positions): a keeper adds reputation and popularity each week, and visitors leave donations.

sigil.label: Binding Sigil
sigil.desc: A demon's reckless drain costs no reputation, and demons in this house take only half as much energy from Sam. Takes no room.

garden.label: Garden
garden.desc: Everyone in the house gains a little mood and rests a little better. Elves get double. Takes no room.

incense.label: Incense Burner
incense.desc: Calm: fewer pushy clients and slower lust. Aphrodisiac: faster lust, bolder ladies, more propositions. Beastkin feel it 60% stronger. Takes no room.

workshop.label: Workshop
workshop.desc: Each dwarf living here (any job) shaves a little off the markup on your next build in this house, up to all of it. Resets after each purchase. Takes no room.

laundry.label: Laundry
laundry.desc: The house gets messy more slowly. Takes no room.

classroom.label: Classroom
classroom.desc: A teacher (one position) drills the house in one subject each week. Choose the subject on the house view or the teacher's sheet.

suite.label: Owner's Suite
suite.desc: Sam's own room in this house. When he sleeps here, his bed is one tier better than the staff's.

lantern.name: The Gilded Lantern
lantern.desc: A classic pleasure house: red velvet, paper lanterns, and a madame who knows everyone in town. Balanced clientele.
lantern.setting: red velvet and gold-trimmed fantasy pleasure house

castle.name: Castle Rosenhal
castle.desc: A crumbling hilltop manor turned discreet retreat for the wealthy. Few guests, very deep pockets, very high standards.
castle.setting: grand old castle chamber with tall windows and faded tapestries

onsen.name: Steamveil Onsen
onsen.desc: Hot springs on the road to the dungeons. Tired adventurers, cheap sake, and a lot of steam.
onsen.setting: wooden onsen inn with paper screens and rising steam

hollow.name: Hollowmere Manor
hollow.desc: Dirt cheap because it's haunted. The ghost is part of the staff now. Customers barely trickle in at first, but thrill-seekers flock once its reputation grows.
hollow.setting: gothic manor room with candelabras, cobwebs and moonlight

tankard.name: The Rusty Tankard
tankard.desc: A tiny tavern with rooms upstairs. Cheap, loud, always busy. Nobles do not come here.
tankard.setting: cramped tavern room above a dockside bar

pavilion.name: Moonlit Pavilion
pavilion.desc: A garden pavilion of music and moon-lilies. Refined, artistic, unhurried.
pavilion.setting: elven garden pavilion with moon-lilies and silk drapes

veil.name: The Crimson Veil
veil.desc: A demon-run den beneath the streets. Anything goes, within reason. Trouble walks in often. Staff get bolder here.
veil.setting: dim underground den with crimson silk and red lanterns

wayfarer.name: Wayfarer's Rest
wayfarer.desc: A caravan inn where every road meets. Travelers pay for room and board, the hearth puts every guest at ease, and there's a steady stream of job-seekers.
wayfarer.setting: cozy roadside inn room with a crackling hearth

skyhook.name: The Skyhook
skyhook.desc: A rowdy lounge bolted to the cliffside airship moorings. Sky-sailors, traders and treasure hunters, all with full purses and short shore leave.
skyhook.setting: lantern-lit airship dock lounge with brass fittings, rope rigging and a view over the clouds

pearl.name: The Pearl Grotto
pearl.desc: A hidden sea-cave bathhouse beneath the harbor, lit by glowing pearls. Very exclusive, very relaxing, and nobody is quite sure who built it.
pearl.setting: luxurious sea-cave grotto with glowing pearls, warm tide pools and carved stone

salaryman.label: Office worker
salaryman.desc: Spreadsheets were his life. Business +20; doing the books saves more.

bartender.label: Part-time bartender
bartender.desc: He can make a cocktail out of anything. Charm +12; tending bar earns 50% more.

gym.label: Gym regular
gym.desc: Thin, but surprisingly strong. Strength +20; recovers more energy.

otaku.label: Isekai otaku
otaku.desc: He has read this story a hundred times. Appraisal starts at Lv 2.

cook.label: Line cook
cook.desc: Staff meals and home cooking. Dinners are free; everyone +2 mood each week.

massage.label: Massage therapist
massage.desc: Good hands, zero experience otherwise. Technique +15; training is more effective.
